senses.gloss: m. (כָּנָה) by-name, surname; attribute, substituted word.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5">Snh. VII, 5</cite> <he>דנין … בכ׳</he> the witnesses are examined by using a substitute for the Divine Name (v. <cite ref="J00217"><he>יוֹסֵי</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 7:6">Sot. VII, 6</cite> <he>במקדש … ובמדינה בכִינּוּיוֹ</he> in the Temple the Divine Name is pronounced as it is written, in the country (outside the Temple) by its substitute (Ădonai).
<cite ref="Sotah 38a:2">Ib. 38ᵃ</cite> <he>בכ׳</he>, opp. <he>שם המפורש</he>; a. e.—Pl. <he>כִּינּוּיִים</he>, <he>כִּינּוּיִין</he>, <cite ref="K00567"><he>כִּנּ׳</he></cite>.

Ned. I, 1 כִּינּוּיֵי נדרים words used as substitutes for vows (נדר); ib. 2 כ׳ לחרם substitutes for ḥerem (v. חֵרֶק); a. fr.—כִּינּוּיֵי כִּינּוּיִין secondary substitutes, e.g. the use of g’rog’roth for tirosh and this for eshkol, v. גְּרוֹגֶרֶת.
<cite ref="Tosefta Nazir 2:1">Tosef. Naz. II, 1</cite>; Y. ib. II, beg. 51ᵈ
